Coefficient inference after sparse selection

Source: R/coefficient_inference.R, R/posterior_sampling.R
coefficient_inference.Rd

Optional posterior, selected-support or case-bootstrap uncertainty summaries for ordinary GLMs, negative binomial, multinomial and Cox models. Request these calculations through summary(fit, inference=...). simulate(fit) and simulate(posterior) return posterior coefficient draws in the original coefficient dimensions.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'L0glm_fit'
simulate(object, nsim = 1L, seed = NULL, control.inference = list(), ...)

# S3 method for class 'L0glm_posterior'
simulate(object, nsim = 1L, seed = NULL, control.inference = list(), ...)

# S3 method for class 'L0glm_posterior'
print(x, digits = 4L, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted L0glm_fit model, or an inference object of class L0glm_posterior returned by summary(fit,inference="posterior")$inference.

nsim

Number of posterior coefficient draws. The simulation methods return coefficient draws, with excluded entries fixed at zero.

seed

Optional random seed; preserves the caller's random-number state.

control.inference

Named inference controls described below.

...

Reserved; unused arguments are rejected.

x

A conditional posterior object.

digits

Significant digits for printed posterior summaries.

Details

With inference="posterior", the selected support and fitted noise parameters are held fixed. When an accepted full support refit supplies the returned estimates, or lambda=0, the calculation uses a flat prior on the admitted coefficients. Otherwise it freezes one adaptive-ridge prior update at the fitted coefficients. In original units its precision is \(P_{jj}=s_j^2\lambda/(4u_j^2)\), where \(u_j=s_j\widehat\beta_j\) is the normalized coefficient. Shared row or predictor-group penalties use their corresponding squared block norms and group multipliers. Mandatory terms have zero prior precision; supplied prior.mean values give the prior centres. Starting exclusions and the selected support remain fixed.

The conditional target is $$p(\beta_J\mid y,J,P,\widehat\psi)\ \propto \exp\{\ell(\beta_J,\widehat\psi) -\tfrac12(\beta_J-c)^T P(\beta_J-c)\}\,1_{\mathcal C}(\beta_J).$$ A separate fixed-prior Fisher-scoring solve finds its constrained mode. The original fitted coefficients and predictions are preserved. The local Gaussian uses precision \(Q=\mathcal I+P\), where \(\mathcal I\) is the IRLS information; multinomial and Cox use joint likelihood information. At a constrained mode \(b_*\), the negative log-target gradient \(g_*\) can be nonzero. The approximating normal therefore has centre \(b_*-Q^{-1}g_*\) and covariance \(Q^{-1}\), truncated to the coefficient constraints. Multinomial draws lie in the admitted zero-sum CLR subspace.

Gaussian identity models with fixed dispersion give the exact frozen-prior Gaussian target, subject to any truncation. Other families use a local likelihood approximation. Quasi families use the corresponding working posterior. Estimated dispersion and NB shape are plug-in values. The method reports posterior means, standard deviations and equal-tail credible intervals, together with the selected estimates and conditional modes. These intervals condition on data-dependent selection and prior estimation; their frequentist coverage after selection can be substantially below the nominal level. Case bootstrapping repeats selection when that variability is of interest.

Sampling uses Cholesky Gaussian draws, independent rejection when the nonnegative region has sufficient probability, and native truncated-normal Gibbs updates otherwise. The full precision is retained in the Gibbs conditionals. Nonnegative draws are sampled from the constrained distribution. Strong posterior correlations can require longer Gibbs runs; use burnin, thin and repeated seeds to assess Monte Carlo stability.

With inference="conditional", the selected coefficients and compulsory terms are refitted without a sparsity penalty, keeping the model family, observation weights, offsets and coefficient constraints. The original fitted object and its coefficients are preserved. Reported estimates and standard errors refer to this selected-support refit. Its original penalized estimates are also retained in the coefficient table.

For ordinary GLMs, the model-based covariance is $$\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\widehat\beta_J) =\widehat\phi(X_J^T W X_J)^{-1},\qquad W_{ii}=w_i\{\mu'(\eta_i)\}^2/V(\mu_i).$$ Supplied fixed dispersion is respected. Estimated dispersion uses the selected-model Pearson scale and residual degrees of freedom. Unknown-scale ordinary-family intervals use a Student t reference; known-scale, negative binomial, multinomial and Cox intervals use a normal reference. NB shape is reestimated when it was estimated in the fit, using plug-in expected coefficient information. Fixed-noise scalar families use observed likelihood information. Cox uses weighted Breslow partial-likelihood information.

Multinomial inference works on the selected zero-sum coefficient subspace. If \(M\) maps independent contrasts into the displayed CLR coefficients, $$\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\mathrm{vec}\widehat B) =M(M^T\mathcal I M)^{-1}M^T.$$ Grouped selection refits the complete CLR rows. Ungrouped selection preserves individual selected CLR entries and the row-sum constraint. Structurally excluded coefficients remain zero. Cholesky inversion uses diagonal equilibration; singular information and coefficients on nonnegative boundaries receive unavailable ordinary Wald standard errors.

These are fixed-model intervals after selection: their nominal interpretation treats the selected model as given. Selection itself contributes uncertainty. Strong-signal settings with reliable support recovery approach the usual fixed-model setting; a finite bootstrap cannot certify perfect support recovery.

With inference="bootstrap", observation rows are sampled with replacement, together with their weights and offsets. Every replicate reruns the saved fitting specification, including its screening, interactions, adaptive-ridge fitting and local refinement. Independent validation data remain fixed. Explicit starting exclusions and externally supplied screening or clustering settings retain their specified meanings. A fit extracted from tuning keeps its chosen lambda; a custom refit callback can repeat tuning as well.

Bootstrap standard errors and percentile intervals include zero estimates in replicates where a coefficient is absent. Selection frequencies are reported for all coefficients selected in the original fit or any replicate. Predictors are retained in every search according to the original fitting specification; there is no pruning based on nonselection in a limited number of replicates. The bootstrap describes variability and selection stability. Discontinuities at selection thresholds can affect nominal interval coverage; see Leeb and Poetscher (2008).

Controls

control.inference is a named list with:

level=.95

Interval probability.

maxit=100L, tol=1e-10

Selected-support refit controls.

max.parameters=1000L, rank.tol=1e-10

Information-matrix dimension guard and numerical rank tolerance.

nboot=199L, seed=NULL

Bootstrap replicate count and optional seed. A supplied seed preserves the caller's random-number state.

nsim=2000L, burnin=500L, thin=1L

Posterior-summary draw count and Gibbs burn-in/thinning. The simulate() methods use their nsim argument. Independent sampling needs no burn-in or thinning.

max.cells=5e7

Memory guard for row resampling and dense bootstrap summary blocks. Coefficient draws are stored sparsely.

refit.args=list()

Overrides to the saved fitting options for bootstrap replicates.

refit=NULL

Optional function receiving a fitting-argument list and returning a fitted L0glm model, or a tuning result with fit_best.

Returned quantities

summary(fit)$coefficients retains the original sparse point estimates. With inference requested, summary(fit)$inference$coefficients is the coefficient table, including estimates, standard errors, interval limits and either credible limits, Wald tests or bootstrap selection frequencies. Original row and channel indices identify each coefficient. Conditional inference also returns the selected-support refit, covariance matrices and convergence diagnostics. Posterior output contains prior.source, prior.precision, prior.mean, frozen dispersion/shape, sampler, covariance and sparse coefficient draws. gaussian.covariance is the covariance before truncation; constrained covariance is estimated from the draws. It stores a compact sampling state for simulate(posterior), excluding the training design and response. Draw rows flatten the original coefficient matrix in column-major order; coefficient.dim, coefficient.dimnames and coefficient.index attributes identify the original coordinates. Excluded coefficients have zero draws.

Bootstrap output retains sparse draws, a sparse original-dimension selection.frequency matrix (extended by the union of generated interaction terms), any generated interaction terms and per-replicate diagnostics with failures, convergence, warnings and timings. Draw rows flatten coefficient matrices in column-major order. replicates identifies successful columns; failed fits are reported and excluded explicitly. At least two successful fits are required. Covariance matrices follow the selected terms in each channel's table; multinomial covariance uses column-major CLR order on covariance.rows. Fitted models retain evaluated options in specification, excluding copies of the design and response; engine identifies the fitter.

References

Leeb, H. and Poetscher, B. M. (2008). Sparse estimators and the oracle property, or the return of Hodges' estimator. Journal of Econometrics, 142, 201-211. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2007.05.017 . Robert, C. P. (1995). Simulation of truncated normal variables. Statistics and Computing, 5, 121-125. doi:10.1007/BF00143942 .

See also

model_summary, l0glmFit

Examples

set.seed(51)
X <- matrix(rnorm(200*10),200,10)
y <- 1+2*X[,1]-2*X[,2]+rnorm(200)
fit <- l0glmFit(X,y,intercept=TRUE,lambda="gic")
details <- summary(fit,inference="conditional")
details$inference$coefficients
posterior <- summary(fit,inference="posterior",
  control.inference=list(nsim=1000L,seed=1))$inference
posterior$coefficients
draws <- simulate(posterior,nsim=1000L,seed=2)
matrix(draws[,1L],nrow(coef(fit)),ncol(coef(fit)))
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
uncertainty <- summary(fit,inference="bootstrap",
  control.inference=list(nboot=199L,seed=1))
uncertainty$inference$coefficients
} # }
